Sound analysis does not speak for itself. These pages cover the communication side of data work: defining the message, choosing the right visual form, and designing outputs that lead to decisions rather than merely displaying numbers.

## What You Will Find Here

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}

## From Analysis to Message

- [Communicating with Data](communicating-with-data.qmd) - Defining the objective, identifying an audience's needs, and a WHO / WHAT / HOW framework to apply before choosing a format
- [Turning Data into Impact](turning-data-into-impact.qmd) - Why sound data does not automatically change decisions, and what closes that gap

:::

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}

## Designing Effective Visuals

- [Data Visualization Principles](data-visualization-principles.qmd) - Decluttering, human perception, the data-ink rule, and responsible color
- [Choosing the Right Chart](choosing-the-right-chart.qmd) - A decision reference for matching chart types to messages: table versus graph, comparisons, and maps
- [Dashboards for Decisions](monitoring-dashboards.qmd) - Designing dashboards that start from the decision, use actionable metrics, and read in five seconds

:::

## Getting Started

**New to communicating with data?** Start with [Communicating with Data](communicating-with-data.qmd) to frame your message, then use [Choosing the Right Chart](choosing-the-right-chart.qmd) when you build your next visual.

## Related Resources

- [Creating Visualizations with Python](../python/index.qmd) - Building charts in code with Seaborn and the grammar of graphics
- [About Data Science](../../index.qmd) - Python data analysis, web scraping, and more
